subject.title: feat(agents): rename model- and user-facing scheduler strings to automations

question: Should the scheduler terminology policy require the model to avoid “cron” everywhere, or only when naming the product feature and tool while preserving “cron” for its technical syntax and compatibility identifiers?
rationale: The RFC-linked rename establishes a product vocabulary, but the correct model-facing boundary between brand terminology and technical cron terminology is a durable UX and documentation policy choice.

options.title: Scope the instruction to product naming
options.body: Call the feature and tool “automations,” while permitting “cron” for cron expressions, config keys, RPCs, and retained compatibility commands.

options.title: Keep the absolute wording
options.body: Require the model never to say “cron,” accepting that technical explanations must avoid the established cron terminology.

options.title: Pause the wording slice
options.body: Defer broad model-facing terminology changes until the RFC resolves the permanent product-versus-technical naming rule.

recommendation.title: Scope the instruction to product naming
recommendation.body: Call the feature and tool “automations,” while permitting “cron” for cron expressions, config keys, RPCs, and retained compatibility commands.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the RFC-linked stacked rename proposal and can clarify its intended terminology boundary for maintainer approval.
